C0.quote: we introduce mixed voting rules for PB
C0.note: PB voting rules aggregating approval ballots into collective decisions.

C1.quote: examine how well the resulting rules approximate well-known proportionality axioms such as EJR+
C1.note: Main results are proportionality guarantees (Theorems 1-3) plus an empirical analysis on Pabulib data. The empirical part uses real-world data.

C2.2.quote: We assume approval preferences and let Ai ⊆ P denote
C2.2.note: Approval sets; cost-satisfaction utilities are derived from them.

C2.3.quote: voter i’s satisfaction (or utility) from project p
C2.3.note: Voters are said to have satisfaction functions, and the paper refers to voter preferences.

C2.4.quote: We assume approval preferences and let Ai ⊆ P denote
C2.4.note: Approval sets are described as preferences and the rule is applied directly to them. There is no statement about submission or sincerity.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: Cost satisfaction function: utility equals project cost if approved, 0 otherwise.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Utilitarian welfare and proportionality (EJR+) are evaluated in the theory and experiments.

C5.2.quote: voter i’s satisfaction (or utility) from project p
C5.2.note: Satisfaction is defined directly from the approval sets. There is no statement relating approvals to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters supply approvals but take no modelled action. Their behaviour is not modelled.

ORG.note: The designer composes the rules outside the model; no agent acts.

DES.note: The designer's choice or objective is not modelled explicitly.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: This parallel has the potential to improve the explainability of mixed PB voting rules
the Value-Based method might be preferable, as it gives strong theoretical guarantees
it is often desirable to achieve good outcomes on multiple objectives

C9.1.note: Claims about which rule to prefer and about real-world explainability.

C9.2.note: The preference-for-rule claim about proportional representation of voters needs a statement that approvals equal held preferences. This is not stated. No strategic-behaviour assumption is stated either.

C10.1.note: No statement of a purely procedural reading.
